hero.title: Game awards decided by players, in the open
hero.subtitle: Judges are drawn at random from the community. Every nomination is public, every rule is published before the edition starts, and nobody decides behind closed doors.

signup.title: Judge signup
signup.body: Anyone with a Discord account can apply before the deadline.

draw.title: Public random draw
draw.body: Judges are drawn with a verifiable seed published in advance.

confirm.title: Judges confirm
confirm.body: Drawn judges accept their seat on the site. Seats left open go to substitutes drawn at random.

play.title: Time to play
play.body: Selected judges get time to play the year's games.

nominate.title: Nominations
nominate.body: Each judge ranks their picks per category. Every nomination is public.

reports.title: Nominees and reports
reports.body: The top five per category are announced. Anyone can report a misplaced nominee, and the jury resolves each report.

vote.title: Public vote
vote.body: The community votes for the winners among the nominees.

reveal.title: Winners revealed
reveal.body: Results are published together with the full, auditable vote log.

transparent.title: Transparent
transparent.body: Judges, nominations and tie-break rules are public.

verifiable.title: Verifiable
verifiable.body: The draw and the vote can be checked by anyone.

fair.title: No arbitrary calls
fair.body: Categories and tie-breaks follow published rules, not admin decisions.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Community Game Awards is an open-source, community-run project. This page explains in plain words what we keep about you and how you stay in control of it.

who.title: Who we are
who.body: Community Game Awards is run by volunteers. For any question or request about your data, write to <email>address</email>.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.discord: From Discord, only when you sign in: your user ID, username, display name and avatar. We only ask Discord for the "identify" permission, so we never see your email, servers or messages.
collect.applications: When you apply as a judge: the edition, the date you accepted the terms and the version of those terms.
collect.cookies: Cookies, all strictly necessary: one keeps you signed in (30 days), one protects the Discord sign-in (10 minutes), and one remembers the language you picked.
collect.ip: Your IP address, for about a minute, to limit abusive traffic. It is kept in memory only and never stored.
collect.none: No analytics, no advertising, no tracking. We never sell or share your data.

public.title: What becomes public
public.body: If you are drawn as a judge, your Discord display name and avatar, and every nomination you make, will be published. That openness is the point of these awards, which is why we ask for your explicit consent before you apply.

why.title: Why we use it
why.body: To run the judge signup and the public draw, with your consent, and to protect the service from abuse.

processors.title: Who processes it
processors.body: Discord (sign-in), Vercel (hosting of the website and its API) and Neon (database). They process the data only to provide those services, and their servers may be outside your country.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: Until you delete your account. Deleting it removes everything we hold about you, including your applications.

choices.title: Your choices
choices.withdraw: Withdraw your application while signup is open, from the signup card.
choices.delete: Delete all your data yourself from Account in the main menu. Deletion happens one week later, so you can change your mind; after that it is permanent.
choices.update: Your profile is refreshed from Discord every time you sign in.
choices.contact: For anything else, such as a copy of your data, a correction or a question, write to <email>address</email>.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If this policy changes, this page and its date will be updated, and significant changes will be announced on the site.
